source.title: AAOIFI Governance Standard (GS) 17: Shari'ah Compliance and Fiduciary Ratings of Sukuk and Other Islamic Finance Instruments
source.approved: AGEB meeting no. 33, October 2023 (Appendix A states 4-5 October / 19-20 Rabi' I 1445H; preparation history states 5-6 October / 20-21 Rabi' I 1445H — internal one-day discrepancy in the PDF), approved unanimously
source.effective_date: Ratings of instruments issued on or after 1 July 2023 (effective date precedes issuance date — retrospective by design)
source.companion_standard: Continuation of GS 10 'Shari'ah Compliance and Fiduciary Ratings for Islamic Financial Institutions' — GS 17 repeatedly imports GS 10 requirements

display_card.name: GS 17 — Shari'ah Compliance & Fiduciary Ratings of Sukuk
display_card.one_liner: Tells rating agencies how to rate Sukuk and other Islamic instruments on Shari'ah compliance and fiduciary performance — not just credit — with instrument-type classification, weighted parameters and a suggested iAAAs-to-iCs scale.

applicability.applies_to: Independent rating agencies conducting Shari'ah compliance and fiduciary (SCF) rating engagements on instruments
instruments_in_scope: Sukuk (by IFIs, corporates or governments — anything meeting the Sukuk definition, by whatever name)
Investment management instruments incl. restricted investment accounts (RIA) not registered as separate legal entities
Unrestricted investment accounts (URIA) or classes thereof — when offered by a non-IFI, or by an IFI not rated under GS 10, or rated below target
Any other publicly offered Islamic finance instrument/product (liability, quasi-equity or asset product)
applicability.recommended_not_mandatory: Highly recommended (not mandatory) for all publicly offered instruments except those from IFIs already rated under GS 10; preferably updated annually and announced publicly (para 6, BC21-BC23)
applicability.assessment_level: Primarily at instrument level; extends to originator / service provider / trustee functions where the instrument's nature requires (para 3)

eligible_agencies: Licensed credit rating agencies that develop GS 10 + GS 17 capacity and methodology
Specialised SCF rating agencies licensed/recognised, with credit-rating expertise involved (para 8)
Plus GS 10 ethics, quality control, engagement-acceptance and fit-and-proper requirements (para 9); AAOIFI code of ethics (para 10)

side_1_shariah_compliance_and_governance: a. Compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules
c. Corporate governance practices related to Shari'ah governance
side_2_fiduciary_performance_and_capacit: g. Creditworthiness of the originator (where applicable)
two_sided_rating.preferred_practice: Two separate scores/ratings — one for Shari'ah compliance & governance, one for fiduciary responsibilities & capacity (paras 27, 42)

four_instrument_types.1_equity_or_quasi_equity_no_guarantee: Participatory; residual interest; perpetual/convertible; no guarantee or purchase undertaking. Examples: Tier 1 Musharaka/Mudaraba/Wakala Sukuk; off-balance-sheet participatory Sukuk and RIAs; Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek at fair-value transfer (paras 14-17)
four_instrument_types.2_quasi_equity_with_guarantee: Guarantee or purchase undertaking gives promised redemption; recourse first to originator, asset acts more as security. Examples: guaranteed participatory Sukuk; IMB at pre-promised price/gift; hybrids not meeting equity or liability tests; URIAs with ongoing redemption (paras 18-20)
four_instrument_types.3_liability_type: Murabaha, Tawarruq, Salam, Istisna and hybrids where liability component >50% of underlying assets at par AND/OR liability component supplies >66.67% of returns. Classification is NOT a Shari'ah-compliance verdict (para 21 + explanation, footnote refers to SS 59 paras 8/2/2-8/2/3)
four_instrument_types.4_asset_type: Asset-side financing/investment products offered by unrated or under-target-rated IFIs, or by non-IFI entities (e.g. Shari'ah-compliant housing finance where no IFIs exist) (para 23)

benchmark_hierarchies.shariah_principles: 1) AAOIFI Shari'ah standards → 2) jurisdiction regulator's Shari'ah regulations → 3) central Shari'ah board rulings → 4) AAOIFI FASs (Shari'ah-related content) → 5) originator's SSB approvals (para 28)
benchmark_hierarchies.shariah_governance: AAOIFI GSs (esp. GS 12) → IFSB Shari'ah governance standards → jurisdiction RSA regulations (para 30)
benchmark_hierarchies.corporate_governance: IFSB corporate governance → AAOIFI GSs → RSA regulations (para 32); assessed at entity level only, not instrument level (para 35)
benchmark_hierarchies.transparency_disclosure: AAOIFI GSs (esp. GS 12) → AAOIFI FASs (esp. FAS 34 'Financial Reporting for Sukuk-holders') → IFSB → IIFM template documents → RSA regulations (para 37)
benchmark_hierarchies.ethics_values: AAOIFI code of ethics → IFSB conduct-of-business → RSA regulations (para 38)

suggested_weights_table_para_48.shariah_governance_framework: equity/quasi-eq no guarantee 15-20; quasi-eq with guarantee 10-15; liability 10-15; asset 5-10
suggested_weights_table_para_48.asset_quality_returns: equity/no-guarantee 25-30; with-guarantee 15-20; N/A for liability and asset types
suggested_weights_table_para_48.creditworthiness_of_originator: N/A for equity/no-guarantee; with-guarantee 15-20; liability 35-45; N/A for asset type
suggested_weights_table_para_48.kill_switch: Failure in a significant category — particularly compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules — is an OVERALL failure regardless of weighted score (footnote 8, para 53)

suggested_rating_scale_para_54: iAAAs 90+ Excellent compliance — preferred structure, no controversial elements, excellent governance and fiduciary performance
iAAs 80-89 Very good — preferred structure, strong governance, strong fiduciary
iAs 70-79 Good — approved structure free of basic non-compliance, good governance
iBBs 60-69 Highly satisfactory — less-preferred structure, may include some controversial elements, sound governance
iBs 50-59 Reasonable — structure not universally considered compliant but approved; certain material non-compliant elements noted
iCs <50 Unsatisfactory — structure controversial per several international jurists or noteworthy basic non-compliance; weak governance and fiduciary
Scale span suggested 5-10 grades; denominations left to the agency (para 53, BC18-BC19)
core_machinery.tiered_and_jurisdiction_specific: Global vs jurisdiction-specific ratings allowed; jurisdiction ratings may amend/drop hierarchy sources but must: publish the amended hierarchy, carry a three-letter jurisdiction suffix, and NOT claim AAOIFI alignment (paras 45-46)

key_rules_for_assurance: Agency must classify the instrument into one of the four types BEFORE choosing scope, weights and scale (para 13)
Shari'ah-compliance parameter is never diluted: 30-35% weight for every type and a failure there fails the whole rating (paras 25, 48 fn8, 53)

For liability and guaranteed quasi-equity types, repayment/returns evaluated via credit-rating-like methodologies (excluding external factors), with fiduciary element reduced/eliminated on the scale (paras 44, 55)
For asset-type instruments the fiduciary element may be eliminated as irrelevant (para 55)
Agency must define and PUBLICISE consistent weights (para 47) and the rating scale (para 53)
Scope limitations that persist after due effort → agency must consider withdrawing (para 49)
Cannot conclude on suitability of benchmarked parameters → agency MUST withdraw (para 51)
Missing Shari'ah parameters → develop them in coordination with the Shari'ah supervisor(s) (para 50)
Agency must identify the correct Shari'ah supervisor(s) of originator/service provider/trustee for Fatwas and rulings (para 52)
Procedures, documentation, archiving, confidentiality and reporting all imported from GS 10 paras 37-54 and 61-62, suitably amended (paras 57-59)
Trustee capacity to uphold Shari'ah provisions is itself an assessed item (para 31(f))
implications: Formal recognition that conventional credit-rating methodology alone is unsuitable for Sukuk — asset-performance risk and Shari'ah compliance are rating dimensions in their own right (IN5, BC2)
Asset-backed Sukuk (Shari'ah-preferred but excluded by most credit raters) get a rating pathway (BC2)
Creates market pressure ('investors' right to know') rather than regulatory compulsion — adoption expected via peer pressure and market discipline (BC5-BC8, BC23)
Lets an unrated or lower-rated IFI get a single product rated to compete (BC3)
The classification tests in para 21 (50% asset / 66.67% return) give the app a concrete, checkable rule for tagging hybrid Sukuk as liability-type
Ratings hierarchy puts AAOIFI Shari'ah standards above national regulators and above the originator's own SSB — a quiet centralisation of benchmark authority (para 28)
limitations: Ratings are 'highly recommended', not mandatory — board explicitly deferred mandatory status to the future (BC21-BC23)
Rating scale and denominations are only suggested; agencies keep discretion (BC18-BC19)
Jurisdiction-specific ratings may drop AAOIFI sources entirely — they just can't claim AAOIFI alignment (para 46)
Classification criteria in para 21 are expressly NOT a statement of Shari'ah compliance (para 21 explanation)
Instrument classification deliberately diverges from AAOIFI FAS classification: quasi-equity is split in two by guarantee/purchase-undertaking existence (BC24-BC27)
Internal date discrepancy in the PDF for the approval meeting (4-5 vs 5-6 October 2023) — tag needs_check for final assembly
disputes: Issue now vs wait for market development: issued now to lead the market (BC1, BC4)
Market relevance without regulatory push: resolved via peer pressure / market discipline / investors' right to know (BC5-BC8)
Sukuk-only vs all instruments: single standard covering all types, including asset-side products (BC9-BC10)
Which agencies are eligible: credit rating agencies included unconditionally (with capacity-building) despite skill-set differences, to widen adoption (BC11-BC13)
One parameter set for all instruments: rejected — hence the four-type classification (BC14)
Prescribed vs discretionary rating scale: discretion won; scale in the standard is illustrative only (BC18-BC19)
Mandatory vs recommended ratings (public-hearing push for mandatory): kept highly recommended — too few service providers exist yet (BC21-BC23)
Divergence from FAS classifications challenged at public hearing: board kept its split, arguing it is a sub-classification within quasi-equity, not a new taxonomy (BC24-BC27)

timeline_bridge.context: Modern standard. Project approved 24-25 March 2020; preliminary study meetings 2020-2021; exposure draft issued 11 December 2022; four public hearings Feb-Aug 2023; final approval October 2023; issued 22 November 2023; effective retrospectively for instruments issued on/after 1 July 2023.
timeline_bridge.predecessor: GS 10 (institution-level SCF ratings) — GS 17 extends the same rating philosophy from institutions to instruments
timeline_bridge.note_for_app_timeline: Anchor as 2023 in the contemporary standards era; developed with executive input from the Islamic International Rating Agency (IIRA); no classical-period dating applies
